Illuminate

/ih-LOO-muh-nayt/ · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Illuminate means to light up; or, figuratively, to make something clear or easier to understand

One vivid demonstration with glowing test tubes did more to illuminate the reaction than an hour of careful notes.

Worked Example

The documentary set out to illuminate the daily lives of deep-sea fishermen, following one crew through a full storm season.

Here illuminate is figurative: the film 'sheds light' on lives most viewers know nothing about, making an unfamiliar world clear. The same verb also works literally - a lamp can illuminate a room.

How Illuminate Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

brighten

brighten: to make lighter or filled with light

elucidate

elucidate: to make something clear by explaining it

reveal

reveal: to bring something hidden into view

Antonyms

obscure

obscure: to hide or make harder to understand

darken

darken: to make dim or gloomy

How Strong Is It? — explain → dazzle → illuminate

explain vs. illuminate

explain vs. illuminate: A manual can explain each step; a single good diagram illuminates how the whole machine works at a glance.

dazzle vs. illuminate

dazzle vs. illuminate: A reading lamp illuminates the page; a wall of stage lights can outright dazzle the eyes.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — il- (in-)

Prefix — il- (in-): in, into, upon - Latin in-, spelled il- before the letter l

Root — lumin-

Root — lumin-: light - from Latin lumen, luminis

Suffix — -ate

Suffix — -ate: to make or cause - Latin verb-forming suffix

Put it together

Put it together: Put the pieces together and you get 'to put light into' - first literally, shining light on something, and then figuratively, shining light on an idea until it finally becomes clear.

Use the root in a new word: luminary

Use the root in a new word: luminary: The conference honored a luminary of ocean science whose research guided a generation of students.
